title: The Children's Funeral for a Fish

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The children are holding a solemn funeral for a dead fish: join in seriously, or let them do it alone.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) found a beautiful dead fish on the beach this morning, and the children have decided it needs a proper funeral, with songs, a speech and a grave in the sand. (friend) has been asked to come. They are all very serious. (friend) is trying very hard not to smile. What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) stands with the children, head bowed, while (subject) gives a speech about the fish's bravery and beautiful colors. They sing a mourning song with the words slightly wrong. (friend) puts a shell on the grave. The children are deeply satisfied.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) decides it is the children's ceremony, and watches from a distance. They do it perfectly, with a great deal of wailing. Then the tide comes in and takes the fish, and (subject) declares that the sea has accepted it. Everyone agrees this is the best possible ending.
